label: PF Backlog 580
title: Fix durable-state clobber: checkpoint newest-wins reconcile + backlog monotonic guard + pf-item merge driver
body:
## Problem / why
The PF Checkpoint state/sync path (core/state_checkpoint.py) copied the WHOLE durable tree from a session'''s possibly-stale runtime checkout over a fresh branch and git add -A'''d it, so an OLDER snapshot overwrote NEWER backlog items on develop (commit c9c16613 / PR #135): revisions/updated_at went backward, history lines were deleted, BI-PF-1246/1247 lost their epic, BI-PF-1348 lost delivery provenance.
## Goal & value
A stale session can never regress durable backlog state; a regression fails closed at PR time.
## In scope
- checkpoint copies ONLY the session'''s changed durable files, NEWEST-wins for items, union for history
- precheck backlog-monotonic guard (fails on revision/updated_at regression or dropped delivery/epic)
- pf-item merge driver (newest version) for data/backlog/items/*.json
## Acceptance criteria
- A stale checkpoint cannot lower an item revision/updated_at or drop delivery/epic
- precheck fails on any item regression vs the integration base
- merging divergent item files resolves to the newest version

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend core/state_checkpoint.py reconcile to diff runtime vs fresh branch and copy only session-changed files with newest-wins (version then updated_at) and history union; add monotonic check in core/merge_gate.py or core/guardrails.py reusing config/guardrail-policy.json; register a pf-item merge driver script under core/ (or tools/) wired via .gitattributes; surface failures through existing merge_gate precheck.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES: item schema fields (version/updated_at/delivery/epic) stable — assumed present
RELATED: BI-PF-1257 (origin of checkpoint), BI-PF-1285 (stale PR base), BI-PF-1290 (per-worker sync)
conflict_findings: BI-PF-1285/1290 touch state_checkpoint/sync paths — potential concurrent edits; sequence after or coordinate
No known conflict with backlog API components
duplication_findings: BI-PF-1285 addresses stale-base PRs (lifecycle), this targets content-level clobber — complementary, not duplicate
BI-PF-1290 auto-resolves generated docs/counters on merge; item-file merge driver is adjacent but scoped to items
BI-PF-1257 introduced the checkpoint path being fixed — this is the regression fix
analysis.rationale: Directly fixes a confirmed data-loss regression with a clear fail-closed design; all three changes extend existing modules (state_checkpoint, merge_gate/guardrails, git attributes) — reuse-first, no new component. Related items cover adjacent lifecycle concerns but not content-level monotonicity, so duplication risk is low. Priority P1/Must: durable state regression silently loses backlog history.
assumptions: Item JSON carries version and updated_at on develop
Integration base ref is available in the precheck environment
Merge driver runs in the same repo where checkpoint PRs are opened
risks: Merge driver needs explicit git config registration; unregistered repos silently fall back to default
Version field may be absent on legacy items — needs fallback to updated_at/content
Concurrent edits with BI-PF-1285/1290 may conflict in state_checkpoint.py
History union semantics could resurrect logically-deleted lines
evidence: Regression committed as c9c16613 / PR #135; BI-PF-1246/1247 epic loss and BI-PF-1348 provenance loss documented in item body
Candidate modules state_checkpoint.py, merge_gate.py, guardrails.py exist with precheck hooks
missing_info: Which field is authoritative for 'newest' if version ties (updated_at vs content hash)?
Should history union also apply to non-backlog durable files, or items+history only?
Where is the integration base ref defined for precheck (develop vs PR base SHA)?
Merge driver language/location preference (Python module under core/ vs tools/)

context_review.reason: What/why/how and affected file (core/state_checkpoint.py) are all specified with clear acceptance criteria; only the merge-driver registration location (.gitattributes/scripts) is implied, not blocking.
